validatedVersusPlanned.publishedCompleted: The 2025 paper reports a single-eVTOL multi-objective planning study in simulated Atlanta, using steady-state CFD wind fields and modified PPO with baseline and reward-ablation experiments.
validatedVersusPlanned.notEstablishedByDeck: Operational sensor-network assimilation, real-time physics-informed wind inference, lifelong learning, multi-aircraft coordination, flight certification, or field-tested dynamic-wind autonomy are not established by this deck.
validatedVersusPlanned.paperFutureWork: Multi-eVTOL coordination, varied origin–destination demands, joint air-ground studies, and stronger multi-wind generalization are discussed as future work.

knownCautions.source: Flying DNA slide 4 versus EAAI Section 5 p. 14
knownCautions.resolution: The deck uses broad continuously sense/learn/adapt language. The article explicitly states single-wind-field training; retain that limitation.
Do not invent numerical experiments or move the existing table values under a claim of new Flying DNA results.
Ours-all leads four of six metrics among listed methods; TD-MPC2-all has better safety and flight time. Preserve both facts.
57.83 kWh / 20.55 dB all-objective result is distinct from 48.28 kWh / 17.99 dB ablation baseline; no cross-experiment subtraction.

knownCautions.source: EAAI Section 4.4.1 p. 10 and aggregate table rows
knownCautions.resolution: Some prose calls a 375.1% difference a reduction; aggregate denominators differ. Keep existing absolute scenario data and do not introduce those percentage claims.
Preserve adverse cases such as DDPG/D90-4 99.4 vs Direct 52.36 kWh. The paper prose example for TD-MPC2/D270-16 is inconsistent with its numeric row; use the table values.

knownCautions.issue: Seven named winds versus Table 5 subset
knownCautions.resolution: Seven named fields are reported overall; Table 5 contains six unique named conditions and not every cross-product. Do not present full-factorial coverage.
Counts over 50,000 training episodes do not constitute a deployed policy success probability.
Only a concise independently attributed related-work card; no claimed authorship, shared results, adopted implementation, or direct performance comparison.
